two given terms are at least two steps apart, and neither is u₁ when u₁ is asked

arithmetic-context.name: An arithmetic sequence or series in a story
arithmetic-context.summary: A story that is one arithmetic sequence: rows of seats, a yearly wage, an amount that changes by the same step, simple interest, a stack of rows, or data that are nearly arithmetic. u₁ and d come from the story, a table, a graph or a figure. The story decides whether a term, a total, a term number or a judgement is wanted, and ArithmeticSequenceSituation's helpers do the sums.

quantities.name: story
quantities.is: what the terms count, and in what steps
quantities.pick: one of eight sequences (four rising, four falling), five amounts that change each step, three lines of evenly spaced things, three net changes that fall past 0, five data tables or three stacks

quantities.name: u₁, d
quantities.is: the first term and the common difference
quantities.pick: the story's own range: whole numbers, or steps of 0.1 or 0.5 where the story has decimals, so every term ends

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: the term number or the number of terms asked about
quantities.pick: 8 to 40 for a term and 6 to 30 for a total, with the story still positive one term past it

quantities.name: X
quantities.is: a target for a term or a running total
quantities.pick: a round number strictly between two neighbours, with the real n at least 0.1 from a whole number

quantities.name: rate
quantities.is: the rate of simple interest
quantities.pick: 2% to 9% in steps of 0.5%, on a deposit of 400 to 5000 tokens in hundreds

quantities.name: data
quantities.is: the table of a nearly arithmetic story
quantities.pick: 5 to 8 years, a step of the story's size and whole-number noise of up to a third of it; every change has the story's sign, and the changes are not all equal

quantities.name: d estimates
quantities.is: what the data say d is
quantities.pick: (last − first) ÷ gaps, and the gradient of the regression line, exact from the sums

quantities.name: N
quantities.is: the year of a prediction
quantities.pick: 2 to 6 years past the table; for a comment, 1 or 2 past it (near), at least three spans past it (far), or past the story's limit (capped)

quantities.name: crate
quantities.is: the size of a stack's whole crates
quantities.pick: 10, 12, 15, 16, 20, 24, 25 or 30, where a multiple comes within 40 rows and not in the first two

clean: Paper 2 only: every part of this type in the bank is Paper 2
a count or amount that ends is marked exactly; what comes from imperfect data is to 3 s.f.
a target is not a term, and its real n is at least 0.1 from a whole number
in a whole-number test u₁ is not a multiple of d, and n is a decimal that ends within two places
in a story every term asked about is positive; only the net stories have negative terms
the stated limit of a story is passed by both the estimate from d and the regression line's
wrong options read differently to 3 s.f.; a number written to 3 s.f. is clear of a rounding edge

distribution.name: One discrete random variable with its probability distribution
distribution.summary: Pick 3 to 5 values of X and their probabilities, as multiples of k, as a formula P(X = x) = k f(x), or as decimals, so they add to 1. A game variant has prizes and a stake. Every probability, E(X), the probability of any event and the expected number of times it happens in n trials are then known, and any of them can be asked.

quantities.name: x
quantities.is: the values X takes
quantities.pick: 3 to 5 whole numbers in a row, from 0 to 7; a game's prizes are $0 and two or three whole numbers of dollars from 1 to 20

quantities.name: P(X = x)
quantities.is: the probability of each value; they add to 1
quantities.pick: whole multiples of k from 1k to 6k; or k f(x) from a formula (kx, k(x + 1), k(x + 2), kx², k(2x − 1), k(6 − x)); or decimals in steps of 0.05 or 0.1, each from 0.05 to 0.6

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: 1 divided by the sum of the multiples of k
quantities.pick: from 1/60 to 1/6

quantities.name: E(X)
quantities.is: Σ x P(X = x)
quantities.pick: exact: a fraction, or a decimal that ends

quantities.name: event
quantities.is: X = a, X > a, X ≥ a, X < b, X ≤ b, a < X ≤ b or a ≤ X < b
quantities.pick: takes in at least one value and leaves out at least one; a strict end is a value of X, so including it changes the answer

quantities.name: p, q
quantities.is: two unknown probabilities in the table, found from the sum and E(X)
quantities.pick: different decimals from 0.05 to 0.6, with E(X) given exactly

quantities.name: stake
quantities.is: the cost to play a game; the game is fair when the expected gain is 0
quantities.pick: the expected prize, a whole number of cents from $0.50 up

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: the number of trials (spins, days, games)
quantities.pick: a whole number from 20 to 600, with n × P(event) a whole number or ending in .5

clean: 3 to 5 values of X, whole numbers in a row; a game has 3 or 4 prizes, one of them $0
every probability is from 0.05 to 0.6 as a decimal, or a multiple of k from 1/60 to 1/6, and they add to exactly 1
answers are exact, as a fraction or a decimal that ends, and are marked right exactly or to 3 s.f.
an asked event takes in at least one value and leaves out at least one
p and q found from E(X) are different and both from 0.05 to 0.6
a fair stake is a whole number of cents, at least $0.50
an expected number of occurrences is a whole number or ends in .5
no answer or option is on a 3 s.f. rounding edge, and every wrong option differs from the answer to 3 s.f.

cubic.name: One cubic with its gradient, tangents and turning points
cubic.summary: Pick a and the stationary x-values p and q, build f′(x) = 3a(x − p)(x − q), add a constant d, then derive every linked quantity, at the turning points and at a chosen point x₀.

quantities.name: a
quantities.is: leading coefficient of f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d

quantities.name: p, q
quantities.is: the x-coordinates of the stationary points
quantities.pick: integers with p < q and |p|, |q| ≤ 4; a(p + q) even so b is a whole number; p + q even when the point of inflexion is asked

quantities.name: b, c, d
quantities.is: the other coefficients
quantities.pick: b = −3a(p + q)/2, c = 3apq, d a small integer

quantities.name: f′(x)
quantities.is: the gradient function 3ax² + 2bx + c
quantities.pick: 3a(x − p)(x − q)

quantities.name: f″(x)
quantities.is: the second derivative 6ax + 2b
quantities.pick: f″(p) = −3a(q − p) and f″(q) = 3a(q − p), so the signs are opposite

quantities.name: stationary points
quantities.is: (p, f(p)) and (q, f(q)): a local maximum and a local minimum
quantities.pick: from p and q; for a > 0 the left one is the maximum

quantities.name: point of inflexion
quantities.pick: midway between the stationary points

quantities.name: x₀
quantities.is: the point where the gradient, the tangent and the normal are asked
quantities.pick: small integer, not p or q, so f′(x₀) ≠ 0

quantities.name: tangent and normal at x₀
quantities.is: y = mx + c with m = f′(x₀) through (x₀, f(x₀)); the normal has gradient −1/m
quantities.pick: from f(x₀) and f′(x₀)

quantities.name: given gradient
quantities.is: a gradient g reached at two whole-number x-values r and s
quantities.pick: r + s = p + q and g = f′(r), with g ≠ 0

quantities.name: hidden coefficient
quantities.is: b or c written as k, found from the tangent's gradient at x₀
quantities.pick: b only when x₀ ≠ 0

clean: Paper 1: every value exact, and a, b, c, d whole numbers
|b|, |c| ≤ 30, |d| ≤ 9, and |f| ≤ 60 at the stationary points and the point of inflexion
x₀ from −3 to 3 with |f(x₀)| ≤ 60 and 0 < |f′(x₀)| ≤ 40
the normal is asked only where |f′(x₀)| ≤ 6, so its gradient and c have denominators of 6 or less
the two x-values with a given gradient are distinct whole numbers from −5 to 5, and |g| ≤ 60

binomial.name: One binomial random variable X ~ B(n, p) in a context
binomial.summary: Pick n trials and a probability of success p, then a count k (or two, for a range). Every probability, the mean, the variance and the standard deviation are then known, and any of them can be asked, from the numbers or from a story about seeds, filters or batteries.

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: the number of independent trials
quantities.pick: a whole number from 5 to 20 for a probability, up to 60 for a mean or variance, up to 40 when n and p are found from the mean and variance

quantities.name: p
quantities.is: the probability of success on one trial, the same every time
quantities.pick: a decimal in steps of 0.05 from 0.1 to 0.9 (steps of 0.1 where a variance or standard deviation is asked, so it comes out exact)

quantities.name: q
quantities.is: the probability of failure, 1 − p
quantities.pick: from p

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: the number of successes asked about
quantities.pick: a whole number from 1 to n − 1, or from 2 to 4 for 'the kth success'

quantities.name: event
quantities.is: X = k, X ≤ k, X < k, X ≥ k, X > k, a ≤ X ≤ b or a < X ≤ b
quantities.pick: its probability from 0.02 to 0.98 (0.01 to 0.4 for X = k), clear of a rounding edge; at most 6 terms when the working adds them

quantities.name: E(X), Var(X), σ
quantities.is: np, npq and √(npq)
quantities.pick: exact decimals for E(X) and Var(X); σ to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: c, N
quantities.is: a target probability for 'at least one success' (0.9, 0.95 or 0.99) and the least number of trials N that reaches it
quantities.pick: N from ln(1 − c)/ln(1 − p) rounded up, with that quotient at least 0.1 from a whole number, N at most 60

quantities.name: m
quantities.is: the trial the kth success is on
quantities.pick: m from k + 2 to k + 8

clean: Paper 2 only (the bank's binomial parts are all Paper 2): probabilities and the standard deviation are answered to 3 s.f., and E(X), Var(X) and n and p are exact

the trials are independent with the same p, and the story says so
a range or a total that the working adds has at most 6 terms; 'at least' and 'between' are also worked with the complement or cdf values
when n and p are found from E(X) and Var(X), Var(X) < E(X), p is a multiple of 0.1 and n is a whole number

binomial-expansion.name: One bracket (ax^p + b)^n, or nCr on its own
binomial-expansion.summary: Pick the power n, then the bracket, then which term is asked. Every coefficient is a whole number, worked out exactly. The same numbers give nCr, a row of Pascal's triangle, the full expansion or one term.

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: the power, and the row of the triangle
quantities.pick: 2 to 12, by the unknown: up to 7 where a row is read, up to 6 for a coefficient on Paper 1 and 10 on Paper 2

quantities.name: r
quantities.is: nCr's r
quantities.pick: from 2 up to n − 2 for a value, 0 or n for an edge

quantities.name: a, p
quantities.is: the term with x, ax^p
quantities.pick: a from 1 to 3, p of 1 or 2

quantities.name: b
quantities.is: the number in the bracket, a letter, or b/x
quantities.pick: up to 4 in size, either sign

quantities.name: first
quantities.is: whether the number is written first, (3 − 2x) or (2x + 3)
quantities.pick: at random, with a negative only in the second term written

quantities.name: j
quantities.is: how many brackets give the x term, so the term asked is in x^(p·j)
quantities.pick: at least 2, and at least 2 left for the other term

a row read from the triangle is row 7 at most (row 8 shown for reading nC2)

regression.name: Paired data and the line fitted to it
regression.summary: Pick x-values and y-values that lie near a straight line, in a story where the correlation is positive or negative. The means, the regression line of y on x and Pearson's r are then known. The same line is used backwards (a constant from the mean point) and forwards (an estimate at an x inside the data, or from a line given to 3 s.f.).

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: the number of points
quantities.pick: 6 to 9

quantities.name: x
quantities.is: the x-values
quantities.pick: n different whole numbers from 1 to 20, in ascending order

quantities.name: y
quantities.is: the y-values
quantities.pick: whole numbers from 8 to 99 that follow a slope of 0.5 to 4 up or down (down where the story says so), with noise of up to 9 either way, so that 0.8 ≤ |r| ≤ 0.99

quantities.name: x̄, ȳ
quantities.is: the mean point
quantities.pick: Σx ÷ n and Σy ÷ n; both end within two decimal places where the mean point is asked

quantities.name: a, b
quantities.is: the regression line y = ax + b of y on x
quantities.pick: exact from Sxy ÷ Sxx and ȳ − a x̄; both clear of a rounding edge at 3 s.f. where they are asked, and |b| ≥ 1

quantities.name: r
quantities.is: Pearson's coefficient, Sxy ÷ √(Sxx Syy)
quantities.pick: clear of a rounding edge at 3 s.f., and so is r²

quantities.name: x₀, y₀
quantities.is: the x an estimate is made at, and the estimate
quantities.pick: x₀ a whole number strictly inside the data and not in the table; y₀ = a x₀ + b is positive, needs rounding, and differs at 3 s.f. from the estimate made with a and b rounded to 3 s.f.

quantities.name: given line
quantities.is: y = ax + b given to 3 s.f. or fewer, for an estimate
quantities.pick: a from 0.50 to 9.99 and b from 1.5 to 99.9, either sign; x₀ from 5 to 40; y₀ from 5 to 500 and needing rounding

quantities.name: mean point and gradient
quantities.is: a mean point (x̄, ȳ) and a gradient a, to find c in y = ax + c
quantities.pick: a to one decimal place from 0.5 to 4.9 (either sign), x̄ from 2.0 to 15.0 to one place, ȳ from 20.00 to 90.00; c ≠ 0 with 1 ≤ |c| ≤ 150

an estimate is inside the data (interpolation), never an extrapolation

regression-interpret.name: What a regression line says, and how far to trust it
regression-interpret.summary: A table of paired data with units in a story, from which the line y = ax + b, r and the range of x are known. a is read as a rate, b as the value at x = 0, and an estimate is judged by where x lies and how strong r is. quantities.name: story
quantities.is: what x and y are, with their units
quantities.pick: one of eight stories: four with x = 0 in the data (time in use, age, pumping time, time since a delivery) and four with x = 0 far below it (fuel, wind speed, load, price)

quantities.is: the number of points
quantities.pick: 6 to 9, or 8 to 9 when the correlation is weak

quantities.name: x
quantities.is: the x-values
quantities.pick: n different whole numbers in the story's range: 0 to 20 with 0 included, or a range such as 30 to 70

quantities.name: y
quantities.is: the y-values
quantities.pick: whole numbers from 8 to 99, near a line of the story's sign

quantities.name: a, b
quantities.is: the regression line y = ax + b of y on x
quantities.pick: exact from the sums, given to 3 s.f., clear of a rounding edge, with |b| ≥ 1

quantities.name: r
quantities.is: Pearson's r
quantities.pick: 0.9 ≤ |r| ≤ 0.99 when strong and 0.2 ≤ |r| ≤ 0.5 when weak, shown to 2 d.p. where it is given

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: the extra x in an expected change
quantities.pick: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 or 10, within the spread of the data

quantities.name: x0
quantities.is: the x an estimate is made at
quantities.pick: a whole number inside the data and not in the table, or at least half the data's spread beyond it

quantities.name: y0
quantities.is: the y known when the line is solved for x

the stories are not those of the bank

data-summary.name: One discrete data set, as a list or a frequency table, and what summarises it
data-summary.summary: Pick a data set of whole numbers, shown as a list in no particular order or as a table of values and frequencies. quantities.name: x
quantities.is: the values
quantities.pick: whole numbers from 1 to 15 (Paper 1) or 10 to 60 (Paper 2); a list has 5 to 11 values on Paper 1 and 10 to 18 on Paper 2; a table has 4 to 8 distinct values

quantities.name: f
quantities.is: the frequency of each value in a table
quantities.pick: 1 to 7 on Paper 1 (a total of 8 to 24) and 1 to 12 on Paper 2 (a total of 25 to 60)

quantities.name: n
quantities.is: how many values there are
quantities.pick: the length of the list, or the frequencies added

quantities.name: mean
quantities.is: Σx ÷ n, or Σfx ÷ Σf
quantities.pick: Paper 1: a whole number or one decimal place. Paper 2: a number that needs rounding, clear of a 3 s.f. rounding edge

quantities.name: median
quantities.is: the middle value, or halfway between the two middle ones
quantities.pick: an odd or an even n

quantities.name: mode
quantities.is: the value that occurs most often
quantities.pick: one value only, strictly the most frequent, occurring at least twice, and not equal to its own count

quantities.name: Q₁, Q₃
quantities.is: the medians of the lower and upper halves (the median itself left out when n is odd)
quantities.pick: Q₁ < Q₃

quantities.name: k, p
quantities.is: a missing value in a list, or a missing frequency in a table, when the mean is given

quartiles are the medians of the two halves, leaving the median out when n is odd, as the IB's GDCs do
a missing value or frequency makes the mean end in at most one decimal place, and the answer is a whole number

compound-interest.name: Money invested at a nominal annual rate, compounded k times a year

quantities.name: rule

quantities.pick: sum, product, difference or larger number

quantities.name: rel, k

quantities.name: prop

sequence-proof.name: One claim about sequences, as a chain of lines

motion-distance.name: A particle's journey, added up
motion-distance.summary: The motion situation with its velocity integrated: a start, a change in displacement and a total distance, split at each rest. It adds families the base does not have: a velocity with one rest, a quadratic displacement, a straight velocity, a position model, a repeating velocity and two racers. The rest finder, the Paper 2 models and the graph drawing are the base situation's.

quantities.name: A, u, r

quantities.pick: u and r whole, with r − u even, so s(t) has whole coefficients and the top of v is at a whole time

quantities.name: c, q

quantities.pick: c and q whole, T past t = 2q

quantities.pick: whole, with b r² and b j² even, so each leg is a whole distance

quantities.name: s0

quantities.pick: whole, from 1 to 9

optimisation-model.name: One shape or journey with a fixed amount and one free length
optimisation-model.summary: Pick a family and numbers with a clean optimum: a yard or plot against a wall, a cylinder, an open bin, a tray cut from a sheet, a rectangle under an arch, a route off a road or the closest point on a curve. The fixed amount, the free length, the function, its derivatives and the optimum are then all known, and any stage can be asked.

quantities.name: family
quantities.is: the shape or journey
quantities.pick: pen, paddock, can, bin, box, arch, route or closest, as the unknown allows

quantities.pick: so Paper 1 gives an exact optimum, and Paper 2 an awkward one

quantities.pick: from the stationary point

tree-diagram.name: A multi-stage event on a tree, or draws from a tin

It adds trees of 2 or 3 branches at each fork and tins that change between draws; the fit test, the colours and the answers are the base situation's.

types.name: Adding up many small pieces
types.summary: Link an area under a curve, a distance from a velocity graph, a normal probability and an arithmetic series as one act of adding up pieces.
types.gap: The exam asks for each total in its own topic; no question asks why a probability is an area or why a series and a trapezium give the same total.

types.name: The nCr pattern
types.summary: Match a row of Pascal's triangle, a term of a binomial expansion and a binomial probability built from the same nCr.
types.gap: The exam asks binomial expansions (topic 1) and binomial probabilities (topic 4) separately and never asks a student to see the same coefficients in both.

types.name: Add and subtract in standard form
types.summary: Add or subtract two numbers in standard form with different powers of ten, and give the answer in standard form.
types.gap: The bank's standard-form parts (t1-standard-form) convert, multiply and divide; none adds or subtracts.

types.name: Powers and roots in standard form
types.summary: Square, cube or take a root of a number in standard form, adjusting the power of ten so that the root comes out whole.
types.gap: The bank's standard-form parts (t1-standard-form) never raise a number in standard form to a power or take its root.

types.name: Sigma notation for arithmetic series
types.summary: Read a sigma sum: count its terms, evaluate it as an arithmetic series, write a series in sigma form, or find the upper limit from the total.
types.gap: In the bank, sigma notation appears only with geometric series (t1-geometric-sequence); no part uses it with an arithmetic series.

types.name: Real value after inflation
types.summary: Find the real value of an investment by using the interest rate minus the inflation rate, and decide whether it keeps up with prices.
types.gap: None of the 16 compound-interest parts in the bank (t1-compound-interest) adjusts for inflation.

types.name: Integer exponent laws
types.summary: Simplify products, quotients and powers of terms with integer exponents, including zero and negative ones, and write a/xⁿ as ax⁻ⁿ.
types.gap: Index laws are used as steps inside calculus and log questions; no bank part tests them on their own.

types.name: Logs and exponential equations on the GDC
types.summary: Evaluate log and ln values on the GDC and solve aˣ = b to 3 significant figures, choosing the right log key.
types.gap: The bank uses the GDC for logs only as a step inside model and finance questions; no part asks for it on its own.

types.name: Identities and unknown constants
types.summary: Tell an identity from an equation, and find the constants that make two expressions identical by comparing coefficients or substituting values.
types.gap: Bank proofs (t1-algebraic-proof) go from one side to the other; none asks for unknown constants in an identity or what ≡ means.

types.name: Numerical "show that"
types.summary: Complete a "show that" with a given number, setting out each step so that the given answer is reached rather than assumed.
types.gap: Show-that lines occur across the bank but are tagged with the skill they show; writing one is never a type of its own.

types.name: Exponential equations with a common base
types.summary: Solve an exponential equation exactly by writing both sides as powers of the same base and equating the exponents.
types.gap: The bank's exponential equations are solved with logarithms (t1-solve-exponential); none is set up for a common base.

types.name: Solve log equations and reject roots
types.summary: Combine logs into one, rewrite in exponential form, solve, and reject any root that makes a log argument zero or negative.
types.gap: Log equations in the bank sit inside Functions types (a log of a quadratic, a hidden quadratic) and carry Functions skills; no topic-1 type covers solving them.

types.name: Exponential equations that are quadratics
types.summary: Spot that an equation in b²ˣ and bˣ is a quadratic in u = bˣ, solve it, and reject any u that is zero or negative.
types.gap: The bank's disguised quadratics are catalogued once, under fn-solve-quadratic with SL2.7.hidden-quadratic, so this topic-1 skill has no type of its own.

types.name: Partial sums against the sum to infinity
types.summary: Compare S_n with S∞: find the least n that brings S_n within a given gap of S∞, or the share of S∞ that the first few terms give.
types.gap: Bank sum-to-infinity parts (t1-sum-to-infinity) find S∞, test convergence or find an unknown; none compares a partial sum with S∞.

types.name: Constant term when both terms contain x
types.summary: In an expansion such as (x² + 3/x)ⁿ, write the general term, find the r that makes the power of x zero (or a given power), and find that term.
types.gap: Bank binomial parts (t1-binomial-term, t1-binomial-find-unknown) have x in one term only; none needs the powers of x from both terms balanced.

types.name: A coefficient in a bracket times an expansion
types.summary: Find one coefficient in (p + qx)(a + bx)ⁿ by pairing each term of the first bracket with the matching term of the expansion and adding.
types.gap: No bank binomial part multiplies the expansion by another bracket.

types.name: A height from two angles of elevation
types.summary: Find a height from two angles of elevation taken a known distance apart, with two right-angled triangles or with the sine rule in the triangle between them.
types.gap: Bank elevation parts (t3-right-angle-trig, t3-bearings-elevation) use one observation point; none needs two.

types.name: Exact lengths and areas in triangles
types.summary: Use exact values such as sin 60° = √3/2 in the cosine rule or ½ab sin C to give a side or an area as an exact surd.
types.gap: Bank triangle parts (t3-sine-cosine-rule, t3-triangle-area) give decimal answers; none asks for an exact surd from exact trig values.

types.name: Population, sample and randomness
types.summary: Name the population and the sample in a study, and decide with a reason whether the sample is random.
types.gap: Bank sampling parts (t4-sampling) ask for the technique or for bias; none asks to name the population and the sample.

types.name: Discrete or continuous
types.summary: Classify a variable as discrete or continuous.
types.gap: No bank part asks for it; it is assumed whenever a chart or a distribution is chosen.

types.name: Numbers in a stratified sample
types.summary: Find how many to select from each group in a stratified sample, as the group's share of the population times the sample size.
types.gap: Bank sampling parts (t4-sampling) name the technique; none works out the numbers for each stratum.

types.name: Frequency tables and histograms
types.summary: Read and complete a frequency table and an equal-width histogram: a missing frequency, a bar height, or how many values fall in a range.
types.gap: Bank data-presentation parts use cumulative frequency graphs and box plots (t4-cumulative-frequency, t4-box-plot); none uses a histogram.

types.name: Describe correlation
types.summary: Describe the correlation in a scatter diagram or from a value of r (direction and strength), and say why correlation does not show cause.
types.gap: Bank regression parts compute r on the GDC (t4-regression-gdc) or interpret the line; describing correlation in words is not catalogued as a type.

types.name: Mutually exclusive events
types.summary: Decide with a reason whether two events are mutually exclusive, and use P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) when they are.
types.gap: Bank Venn parts (t4-venn-addition-rule) use the general addition rule; none asks whether events are mutually exclusive.

types.name: Conditional probability from a diagram
types.summary: Read a conditional probability straight from a two-way table, Venn diagram or tree by keeping only the given group.
types.gap: Bank conditional parts are catalogued under t4-conditional-probability with the 4.11 formula skills; reading the condition off a diagram is not a type of its own.

types.name: Find, interpret and compare z-scores
types.summary: Find a z-value and say what it means, turn a z-value back into x, and compare results from two different normal distributions using z.
types.gap: Bank parts use z only as a step to an unknown mean or standard deviation (t4-normal-unknown-parameter); none asks what a z-value means or compares two.

types.name: From chords to the tangent
types.summary: Find the gradients of chords from a point to nearby points, see them approach a limit, and give that limit as the gradient of the tangent.
types.gap: Bank derivative parts (t5-derivative-meaning) interpret a derivative or estimate a limit; none builds the gradient from chords.

types.name: Estimate a gradient from a graph
types.summary: Estimate the gradient of a curve at a point from a drawn tangent or with the GDC, and compare the gradients at two points.
types.gap: Bank gradients come from differentiating a formula; none asks for an estimate from a graph.

types.name: Increasing or decreasing at a point
types.summary: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing at one point from the sign of f′ there, and give the reason.
types.gap: Bank parts ask for the intervals where f increases or decreases (t5-increasing-decreasing); none asks about a single point.

types.name: Show a function always increases
types.summary: Show that f′(x) > 0 (or < 0) for every x in the domain, for example because f′ is a square plus a positive number or a positive exponential.
types.gap: No catalogued bank part asks for this proof on its own.

types.name: Counting: codes, arrangements, selections and restricted rows (AA HL)
types.summary: Count outcomes with the multiplication principle, ordered arrangements with n! and nPr, selections with nCr (exactly, and 'at least one'), and rows where two people must or must not sit together.
types.gap: The question bank behind the exam types is AA SL's, which has no counting parts. AHL1.10's counting skills are AA HL only, so there is no bank part to hang them on: this type is built from the HL syllabus map and its exam-style prompts.
types.examStyle: AA HL papers ask these counts in words: a code, medals among runners, a committee with exactly or at least one of a kind, two people together or apart in a row. Every unknown is one of those questions, so with Exam-style only on an AA HL student gets each of them in words. The bare-symbol drills (evaluate 10P3) are practice, not exam style, so the equation representation stays out.
